samples.summary: New Remove-link toolbar button has no test at all, yet the diff argues it is the only way to drop a hyperlink in Slides
samples.evidence: The diff adds `showRemoveLink` plus a `Remove link` ToolbarButton wired to `editor.removeLink?.()` + `editor.focus()`, and opts it in from `text-edit-section.tsx` and `mobile-toolbar.tsx`. Nothing asserts the button renders under `showRemoveLink`, that it is absent by default (docs), or that clicking it calls `removeLink`. A jsdom render harness for exactly this component already exists (`packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/text-format-toggles.test.ts` renders `TextFormatGroup` with a mock `TextFormattingEditor` and clicks `[aria-label=...]` buttons), so coverage was cheap. `packages/frontend/tests/app/slides/toolbar/text-edit-section.test.ts` only smoke-imports the module and structurally checks method names on a mock; `mobile-text-toggles.test.ts` mocks `removeLink: vi.fn()` but never clicks it. Since Clear formatting now deliberately preserves `href` and Slides has no link popover, a regression (button missing, mis-labelled, wrong callback, missing `data-text-edit-keepalive` so the text box commits/blurs before the click lands) leaves Slides users with no way to remove a link and nothing in CI notices.

samples.summary: Slides text-box clear-formatting test passes even if nothing happens — no pre-assertion that the formatting was ever applied
samples.evidence: `keeps the href while clearing the formatting on the same run` does `insertLink` → `selectAll()` (a synthetic Ctrl/Meta+A keydown) → `applyStyle({bold, color})` → `clearInlineFormatting()`, then asserts href present and every run's bold/color falsy. `applyStyleImpl` in `packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:819-820` returns immediately when there is no selection, and `clearInlineFormatting` (line 1077-1082) routes through it, so if the select-all keydown ever stops selecting (focus, platform mod detection at text-editor.ts:1039-1040, handler ordering) both calls become no-ops and all four assertions still hold: bold/color are falsy because they were never set, and href survives because nothing was written. The test then proves nothing about `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` on this surface. An intermediate `expect(...)` that bold/color are actually present before clearing (or setting the styled run in the initial `blocks`) would make it fail-capable.

samples.summary: The helper's widened block lookup (getBlock→findBlock, i.e. header/footer/table-cell reach) is untested
samples.evidence: The extracted `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` swaps the old `try { this.doc.getBlock(...) } catch { return false }` for `doc.findBlock(position.blockId)`, and the comment explicitly claims new reach: 'a caret in a header, footer or table cell resolves too'. That is a behavior change for `exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge` (link exit on Space/Enter previously no-opped in those contexts) as well as for both Clear-formatting entry points. Every new test places the caret in a top-level body paragraph: `link-trailing-edge.test.ts` uses `createEmptyBlock()` body blocks, `editor-clear-formatting.test.ts` a single body paragraph, `text-box-clear-formatting.test.ts` a text box (no headers/tables at all). No test exercises a link trailing edge inside a table cell or header/footer, so neither the new reach nor a possible regression in it is detected. There is also no direct unit test of the exported helper (`packages/docs/test/model/` contains only `caret-style-surface.test.ts`, which never mentions href).
searchedFor: read both new/updated docs view tests

samples.summary: The `prev.href === undefined` half of the new `exitsLink` condition is never exercised on its own
samples.evidence: Both entry points compute `exitsLink = isAtLinkTrailingEdge(...) || !!(prev && 'href' in prev && prev.href === undefined)` (editor.ts ~3363-3370 and text-editor.ts ~3438-3448). In every new test the caret is literally at the link's trailing edge, so the first disjunct is already true and the pending-style re-check contributes nothing; no test sets up a pending `href: undefined` at a position where `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` is false (the scenario the comment says the clause exists for). The clause is therefore either untested defensive code or untested extra reach — a case where clearing would arm a link exit the caret position does not justify would go unnoticed.

samples.summary: Collapsed-caret Clear formatting is only asserted on `href`; the newly widened cleared-key set on that path is untested
samples.evidence: `TextEditor.clearFormatting` now pends `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` instead of its old hand-rolled list, adding fontSize/fontFamily/color/backgroundColor to what the collapsed caret clears (per the new doc comment). The collapsed-caret tests in `link-trailing-edge.test.ts` (`Cmd+\ at a link trailing edge…`, `Cmd+\ inside link text…`, and the two Clear-formatting-button cases) type a character and assert only `style.href`; none asserts that the typed run came out plain (e.g. bold/color/fontSize cleared). The range-path shortcut test in `editor-clear-formatting.test.ts:191` asserts only `bold` and `color`, not `fontSize`/`fontFamily`/`backgroundColor`. So a regression in the pending key set (or a later re-drift of the shortcut) would keep the suite green.

finding.evidence: The diff adds `showRemoveLink` plus a `Remove link` ToolbarButton wired to `editor.removeLink?.()` + `editor.focus()`, and opts it in from `text-edit-section.tsx` and `mobile-toolbar.tsx`. Nothing asserts the button renders under `showRemoveLink`, that it is absent by default (docs), or that clicking it calls `removeLink`. A jsdom render harness for exactly this component already exists (`packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/text-format-toggles.test.ts` renders `TextFormatGroup` with a mock `TextFormattingEditor` and clicks `[aria-label=...]` buttons), so coverage was cheap. `packages/frontend/tests/app/slides/toolbar/text-edit-section.test.ts` only smoke-imports the module and structurally checks method names on a mock; `mobile-text-toggles.test.ts` mocks `removeLink: vi.fn()` but never clicks it. verdict.reason: The Remove-link button exists in text-format-group.tsx (showRemoveLink prop default false at :102, handler at :174-178, ToolbarButton aria-label="Remove link" at :310-325) and is opted into by text-edit-section.tsx:93 and mobile-toolbar.tsx:580, but no test anywhere exercises it. All three jsdom suites that render TextFormatGroup (text-format-toggles.test.ts, toolbar-focus.test.ts, color-reset.test.ts) omit it: toolbar-focus.test.ts:121 iterates Bold/Italic/Underline/Strikethrough/"Insert link" only, :130 checks keepalive only for the two color triggers, and :140-154 asserts the showStrikethrough/showHighlight omissions with no showRemoveLink analogue; its mock editor (:39-53) does not even stub removeLink. The slides toolbar tests are no better: text-edit-section.test.ts is state-machine logic plus an import smoke test (:226-231) and a typeof structural check (:193-218) that does not list removeLink; mobile-text-toggles.test.ts stubs removeLink (:71) but its CASES (:124-128) never click it. Repo-wide case-insensitive searches for "Remove link"/"unlink", "showRemoveLink" and "IconUnlink" match no test file, there is no e2e spec directory, and the only snapshots are core tokens and slides shape registry. Since Clear formatting deliberately preserves href and Slides has no link popover, an untested regression here leaves users with no way to remove a link — major.

finding.summary: New Remove-link toolbar button (showRemoveLink) has no test at all, though it is now the only way to drop a hyperlink in Slides
finding.evidence: The diff adds a `showRemoveLink` prop, an `IconUnlink` ToolbarButton (aria-label "Remove link") and a `handleRemoveLink` callback in text-format-group.tsx, and opts it in from `text-edit-section.tsx` and `mobile-toolbar.tsx`. No test asserts (a) the button renders only when `showRemoveLink` is passed, (b) clicking it calls `editor.removeLink()` and re-focuses. `packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/text-format-toggles.test.ts` already provides exactly the needed jsdom + createRoot + `[aria-label=...]` harness for TextFormatGroup, so such a test was cheap; `tests/app/slides/toolbar/text-edit-section.test.ts` only does state-machine checks plus a module-import smoke test (`expect(typeof mod.TextEditSection).toBe("function")`) and merely stubs `removeLink: () => {}`. Since Clear formatting no longer removes hyperlinks (#1051) and slides has no link popover, a silently unrendered or unwired button leaves users with no way to remove a link, and nothing in CI would catch it (frontend has no tsc, and JSX props like a typo'd/never-passed flag fail silently).

verdict.reason: The Remove-link toolbar button is real code (text-format-group.tsx:72,102,174-178,310-325) opted into by the slides text-edit toolbar (text-edit-section.tsx:22), yet no test anywhere renders TextFormatGroup with showRemoveLink, queries [aria-label="Remove link"], or asserts that clicking calls editor.removeLink() and re-focuses. The closest harness, toolbar-focus.test.ts:120-155, asserts exactly this style of flag-gated rendering for showStrikethrough/showHighlight and mousedown behavior for Insert link, but omits Remove link entirely. Repo-wide grep for the literal "Remove link" in code files hits only the two source components; case-insensitive grep for removeLink across all test/ and tests/ dirs hits only editor-model tests (packages/docs/test/view/*, packages/slides/test/view/editor/text-box-editor.test.ts:740 which merely checks typeof) and inert mock stubs (mobile-text-toggles.test.ts:71, text-edit-section.test.ts:37, docs-link-popover.test.tsx:26 which tests the separate docs popover). I also followed the indirect route: the visual harness scenario slides-toolbar-text-editing renders the component, but the checked-in baseline PNG I opened is cropped at the Bold button and contains no link cluster, so it gives no coverage of rendering, and a screenshot cannot cover the click wiring. No e2e suite exists. This is a missing test over a new user-facing path — the component's own comment states this button is Slides' only way to drop a hyperlink — so it is blocking at major under the test-adequacy rubric.

finding.summary: Text-box `clearInlineFormatting` collapsed-caret-at-link-trailing-edge case is untested (and lacks the override the docs path got)
finding.evidence: `TextBoxEditorAPI.clearInlineFormatting` still calls `applyStyleImpl(CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE)` with no trailing-edge `href: undefined` override — the addition the diff made only to `EditorAPI.clearInlineFormatting` (editor.ts:3366) and `TextEditor.clearFormatting`. The new test file `packages/docs/test/view/text-box-clear-formatting.test.ts` only covers a select-all range clear and `removeLink`; it never places a collapsed caret at a link's trailing edge, clears, and types. The docs counterpart deems exactly that scenario a defect ('the next typed character would silently extend the link') and covers it in link-trailing-edge.test.ts, but the slides/text-box equivalent (`text-box-link-trailing-edge.test.ts` covers only Space/Enter) has no such case, so link extension via the Slides Clear-formatting button ships with no coverage.

verdict.reason: The finding's factual core (no text-box test for collapsed caret at a link trailing edge + clear + type) is true, but its blocking premise is not. The docs link-extension bug arises because docs `applyStyleImpl` writes `pending.set({...caretStyle, ...style})` at a collapsed caret (editor.ts:1167-1174), overwriting the `href: undefined` armed by `exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge` — hence the override at editor.ts:3344-3373 and text-editor.ts:3426-3450. The text-box `applyStyleImpl` early-returns at a collapsed caret (text-box-editor.ts:819-821) and never touches `pending`, so the armed link exit (wired at text-box-editor.ts:708, armed at text-editor.ts:5912-5916) survives the Slides Clear-formatting button; the asserted defect ("next typed character silently extends the link") is structurally impossible on this path. That no-op is itself asserted at text-box-editor.test.ts:43-47, and the behavior the diff actually changed for text boxes (href kept through clear, removeLink still drops it) is genuinely exercised end-to-end in text-box-clear-formatting.test.ts:111-134 with no over-mocking. So this is a wish for an extra regression guard over an unchanged, failure-proof path — nit/minor at most, not a major test-adequacy blocker; the docs/slides API asymmetry is a correctness-lens matter.
